case_title: Kashmira Devi v. State of Uttarakhand & Ors.
evidence_type: Dying declaration, medical evidence, witness testimony
aggravating_circumstances: Dowry harassment, cruelty, unnatural death within seven years of marriage
mitigating_circumstances: Appellant's age, contribution to family, husband's age
high_court_outcome: Convicted under s.304-B and s.498-A IPC, awarded life imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused, a mother-in-law, was involved in the death of her daughter-in-law, who died from severe burn injuries. The victim, who was married to the accused's son, had been subjected to harassment and cruelty by her in-laws for dowry demands. The victim returned to her parental home after being harassed, but was sent back to her matrimonial home by her in-laws. The victim was later found burned and died from her injuries. The prosecution presented multiple dying declarations from the victim, which were recorded under various circumstances, including the presence of the accused and her husband. The trial court acquitted the accused, but the High Court convicted her under sections 304-B and 498-A of the IPC, citing the presumption of dowry death under the Evidence Act. The Supreme Court upheld the conviction but modified the sentence to rigorous imprisonment for seven years.
